text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Thursday.
- Pension reforms will hit unemployed and sick. Pensions look set to fall by up to 10 percent according to current plans.
- Health insurance firms have recovered better than expected. Their debt of 3.6 billion schillings in 1995 has shrunk to 94 million schillings.
- The lack of apprenticeships remains an acute problem.
- A child porn ring was able to keep going because people turned a blind eye on suspicious behaviour.

- Bank Austria head Gerhard Randa sees dividend bonus in sight. If the results do not turn out much worse in the second half than in the first, a bonus will be paid on top of the 12 percent base dividend paid in 1996.
- Family Minister Martin Bartenstein is not considering a ban on sects such as Scientology yet.
- Due to lower savings rates Austrians are snapping up securities like hotcakes, and so are foreigners. The foreign travel boom is ebbing which has helped the current account deficit somewhat.
- Petrol prices are being hiked again. Criticism of oil firms which are raising prices by up to 0.3 schillings.
- Farmers will receive 72 billion schillings in subsidies from the European Union over three years (including 1997). However, they are still far off the world market.
- Styrian wire producer Pengg-Gruppe is facing insolvency due to competition from Stahlcord in Fuerstenfeld.
- The future of involvent Eduard Oberndorf hosiery factory is in the balance.
- Debate over duties of federal president ahead of presidential election campaign. Social Democrat politician Josef Cap thinks President Thomas Klestil should propose a reduction of his duties.
- Sharp criticism of the budget policies of Burgenland province. Need for strong action in consolidation of budget.
